svg.title: Past search schematic 05: where the recorded searches were, against the atlas's candidate places
svg.text: Past searches 05 — where the recorded searches were, against the atlas's candidate places
Three maps to scale, north up, from WGS84 lat/lon (equirectangular, x scaled by cos latitude). No base map: the repo has no Dead Sea or Jordan outline.
36 places with coordinates; in A and B, dots only.
Off this frame (from the Temple enclosure):
Tombs of the Kings, 1.3 km NNW
A — Jericho, Qumran and the desert, enlarged
Every ledger search that can be placed lies here, except S07 and S08 at Mount Gerizim.

README; research/models/search_effectiveness/looks.csv, results.json and README §5; WGS84 points from
WGS84 lat/lon, 111.32 km per degree, x scaled by cos latitude at each map's centre; a bar on each
map. Rows with no WGS84 point in the repo sit at their place's atlas point. No datum transform.
Of 39 candidate places, 4 have a ledger search; 2 of those are “near” matches only. Only Kh. Qumran
has a scroll-motivated one. 32 places, all of Jerusalem among them, have nothing. No look at any
candidate place has a detection probability.
This sheet identifies nothing; it shows coverage of the record only. A marker does not mean the place
was covered: no row has a target volume, and the negative rows (S03, S10, S17) have unknown or tiny
